Df4sSeUMDed.caption:
🇲🇹🇯🇵🇨🇼 Meet the Miss International contestants!

We asked three delegates about their work and their message for the competition ✨

🇲🇹 Malta nikole_buhagiar 
A student working toward her bachelor's degree at Cambridge. Her message: "No matter how hard it is to compete, we should all remain as sisters, equally united."

🇯🇵 Japan michiru_yakuma
An M&A consultant. "I'm very excited to represent Japan and to meet friends from around the world."

🇨🇼 Curaçao samiahbooi
A master's student in international business law. Her message: "Authenticity is the most important thing. Be yourself and enjoy every second of this experience."

🇲🇹🇯🇵🇨🇼 ミス・インターナショナル出場者を改めてご紹介！

各国を代表するミスに、お仕事と大会へのメッセージを聞きました✨

🇲🇹 マルタ nikole_buhagiar
ケンブリッジで学士号の取得に向けて勉強中の学生です。「どれだけ競い合うのが大変でも、みんな姉妹のままで。対等に団結していたい」とコメントしてくれました。

🇯🇵 日本 michiru_yakuwa 
M&Aコンサルタントとして活躍中。「日本の代表として、世界中の友達に会えることを楽しみにしています」

🇨🇼 キュラソー samiahbooi 
国際ビジネス法の修士課程で学ぶ学生です。「ありのままでいることが一番大切。この経験の一瞬一瞬を楽しんで」とメッセージをくれました。

Df3NusJTkez.caption:
🍁 Discovering Japanese Culture in Autumn 🇯🇵

The Misses visited the Northern Culture Museum in Niigata, Japan!

Once the residence of the wealthy Ito family, the museum showcases traditional Japanese architecture, beautiful gardens, and the rich history of the family.

Surrounded by the beauty of the gardens and historic architecture, the Misses had a wonderful opportunity to experience Japan’s traditional culture and heritage.

It was a special moment filled with the beauty of autumn in Japan! 🍁✨

ミスたちが訪れたのは、新潟県にある「北方文化博物館」！

かつての豪農・伊藤家の歴史を今に伝える、伝統的な日本建築と美しい庭園が魅力の場所です。

四季折々の表情を見せる庭園や、歴史を感じる趣ある建物を通して、日本の伝統文化や美しさに触れるひとときとなりました。

日本の秋ならではの景色とともに、心に残る特別な時間を過ごしました🍂✨

#missinternational 
#japanculture 
#autumninjapan 
#japanesetradition

DfbBIX0xCuq.caption:
Chile meets the Universe 🇨🇱💫

And so we embark on this journey to Miss Universe’s 75th edition with the love and warmth of the Chilean people. I’m ready to not only be seen but heard and leave Chile’s name in the highest regards. Today we start an endeavor that promises to be an experience like no other and I feel calm and prepared to show the universe that beauty lies within us. Thank you for the continuous support and affection. I am determined to do all that I can to bring that second crown home through hard and honest work. 

Thank you to the beautiful dancers of balletalquintacatemu for their wonderful performances ❤️‍🩹

// 

Y así emprendemos este camino hacia la 75.ª edición de Miss Universo, llevando con nosotros todo el amor y la calidez del pueblo chileno. Estoy lista no solo para ser vista, sino también para ser escuchada y dejar el nombre de Chile en lo más alto. Hoy comienza una aventura que promete convertirse en una experiencia única y me siento tranquila y preparada para mostrarle al universo que la verdadera belleza nace de nuestro interior. Gracias por su apoyo incondicional y por todo el cariño que me han entregado. Estoy decidida a dar lo mejor de mí, trabajando con esfuerzo, dedicación y honestidad para traer esa segunda corona a casa.

Her commitment to making a difference goes beyond technology. Since 2022, she has also been volunteering with Community TechAid, helping bring technology and educational opportunities to those who need them most.

Laura believes that while technology continues to evolve, what truly matters is how we care for and support one another. She hopes to inspire a future where innovation and compassion go hand in hand.

Her message is clear: a better future begins when we use our knowledge and creativity to help others.

Isabel Cramer, Miss International Netherlands 2026, is a literary studies master's graduate and fashion designer who aspires to become an author. She hopes to take her creativity further and write a book that inspires many people.

Through her platform "Climate Creatives," Isabel shows that living sustainably can be a creative challenge rather than a burden. With her passion for sewing, she transforms leftover materials into gowns worth cherishing, giving existing resources new life instead of treating fashion as disposable. She believes climate action begins when we feel connected to what we want to protect, and that creativity is the bridge between caring and doing.

Her message is clear: we are not separate from nature, but a part of it. She wants to help people realize why it matters to build a greener, brighter future for the generations to come.

The beauty queens also highlighted their collaboration with the Government of Zimbabwe and their work with young girls and boys living with disabilities across the African continent.

Vice President Ansah welcomed the initiative and commended the beauty queens for the impactful work they are doing.

She described them as icons and good leaders who are serving as positive role models for young people in their respective countries.

Miss Universe Philippines Takes Home the Icon of Excellence in Pageant Organization Award! 🏆🇵🇭

A recognition worthy of the legacy we continue to build. Miss Universe Philippines proudly receives the Icon of Excellence in Pageant Organization award at the 2026 Global Iconic Aces Awards.

Behind every Filipina who steps onto the Miss Universe stage is an organization committed to building her journey beyond the crown. Through years of developing queens who represent the Philippines with distinction, Miss Universe Philippines continues to set its sights on greater heights for Filipino pageantry. This award celebrates that work and the vision that continues to move us forward.

The award was received by MUPH Marketing Lead Ria Panugan on behalf of our President, Jonas A. Gaffud, whose leadership continues to champion meaningful causes and create a lasting impact beyond the pageant stage.

Also present at the event was our partner, TrendyCreation, the award-winning pageant heels brand.

Thank you for this recognition. Miss Universe Philippines will continue to raise the Philippine flag, waving the pride of our nation to every corner of the universe.

Presenting my advocacy project for Miss Universe 2026. “Dare To Be Yourself” is an initiative that stems from my own personal experience with school bullying, an issue that’s still relevant in our classrooms today. Through this project, I aim to reach schools all around Chile and hopefully the world to talk with students about bullying prevention, give them resources to find help if needed and also remind them of the importance of nourishing their essences no matter what others may say.

I was able to rewrite my story with my own words when others tried to do it for me. It is now my dream to inspire children and young people to do the same.

I am so moved to be given this platform to be an actual agent of change. This is just the beginning.

DeNuTkGkcXT.caption:
Recuerdos de mi primera vez en Puerto Rico 🇵🇷 

Qué hermoso día lleno de cultura y goce. Empezamos visitando la Hacienda Muñoz (hacienda_munoz) en San Lorenzo donde aprendí sobre la producción del café de especialidad boricua y también sobre la historia de las fincas en el país. 

Luego nos deleitamos con comida puertorriqueña tradicional en Zafra (zafradelcaribe_ ) donde cada plato hacía bailar al paladar. 

Después visitamos en faro Punta Tuna en Maunabo, un lugar que durante siglos fue la estrella guía de los barcos que llegaban a la isla.

Y finalizamos el día en Río Grande, donde las vistas del imponente Yunque, el único bosque tropical lluvioso en el sistema forestal nacional de Estados Unidos, fueron la imagen perfecta para finalizar el día. 

Gracias cristiandianapr y tiagocristinaa por acompañarme y hacer de este viaje algo aún más memorable 💗 Mañana seguiremos #DescubriendoLaIsla

DdT76ygDgfF.caption:
Meet Miss Universe Canada 2026, Aslihan Morali. 🇨🇦

Aslihan’s journey is one shaped by resilience, opportunity and purpose. After immigrating to Canada from Türkiye as a young girl and being raised by a single mother, she grew up with a deep appreciation for education, perseverance and the freedom to dream beyond one’s circumstances.

Today, she carries that story with her as she prepares to represent Canada on the Miss Universe stage in Puerto Rico.

For Aslihan, the crown represents far more than a title. It is a platform to connect with communities, advocate for education and opportunity, and remind others that where you begin does not determine where you are going.

We are proud to stand behind a Canadian representative who leads with authenticity, kindness and purpose, and we look forward to sharing this journey with all of you as she takes Canada to the Miss Universe stage. 🇨🇦✨

The road to Miss Universe begins now.

DdSA6EfTaj-.caption:
Reliving the crowning of our 2026 Miss Universe Canada, Aslihan Morali! We have no doubt that she will represent Canada proudly at the 75th Miss Universe Canada pageant in November in Puerto Rico ! 

As a child, Aslihan Morali walked across the Buffalo-Niagara bridge into Canada as a refugee with two suitcases and a dream. Today she is a model, humanitarian, and founder of Leap Global Voices, delivering educational resources to children in the Philippines, sponsoring girls’ education in Türkiye, and leading empowerment workshops across Canada. A longtime supporter of the SickKids Hospital Burn & Plastics Gala, trained by world-renowned supermodel Coco Rocha, and guided by faith and purpose, Aslihan proves every day that where you begin never determines where you are going.

Ddc8piryIfW.caption:
✨Durante 75 años, Miss Universe ha construido un legado internacional que ha trascendido generaciones, culturas y fronteras, convirtiéndose en una plataforma para celebrar el liderazgo, la preparación, la belleza y el empoderamiento de la mujer.

Como la Dirección Nacional de Miss Universe Cuba, asumimos con responsabilidad el compromiso de representar y fortalecer esta institución en nuestro país, actuando siempre bajo principios de respeto, integridad, transparencia y responsabilidad.

Nos unimos a la declaración de los Directores Nacionales y expresamos nuestro respaldo a las acciones dirigidas a preservar la estabilidad, integridad y continuidad de Miss Universe Organization. Creemos que cualquier diferencia debe ser abordada responsablemente, a través de los canales correspondientes y procurando siempre proteger el legado y la institución que representamos.

Asimismo, reafirmamos nuestro apoyo a Puerto Rico como sede de la histórica 75.ª edición de Miss Universe, una celebración que marcará el aniversario de diamante de la Organización.

Desde Cuba continuaremos trabajando con el mismo compromiso, respeto y responsabilidad con los que asumimos nuestra representación. missuniverse 

75 años de historia. Un legado que continúa.
Miss Universe Cuba 🇨🇺✨

Df2Gulht7gY.caption:
FROM 1952 TO 2026 – 75 YEARS OF MISS UNIVERSE ✨👑🇩🇰

From the very first Miss Universe competition in 1952, when Hanne Sørensen proudly represented Denmark, to Fie Rose, representing our country at the historic 75th edition of Miss Universe in Puerto Rico.

Two women. Two generations. One dream. 🇩🇰

For 75 editions, Miss Universe has celebrated beauty, confidence, ambition, and the power of women from around the world.

Today, we honor Denmark’s journey through the decades, from where it all began to the incredible women who continue to carry our flag onto the international stage.

Different eras, the same Danish pride.

As Fie Rose takes part in this milestone edition, we celebrate the past, embrace the present, and look forward to the future of Miss Universe Denmark.

A legacy that began in 1952. A story that continues today✨

De2W3lXsHn2.caption:
Every child deserves to know: I matter. I belong. My future holds possibilities.

For Miss Universe Estonia, Emili Denneng, this is personal. Having experienced bullying herself, she knows how much it matters to feel accepted and believed in.

Kambuka is a youth club in Estonia that organizes camps and activities where children can find friends, discover their strengths, and feel free to be themselves. A place where “Can I join?” becomes “We’re so glad you’re here.”

But some families cannot afford that opportunity. Emili wants to help change this.
Your support can help cover a child’s participation. Your time and skills can help them feel heard and encouraged.

We cannot erase what a child has been through. But together, we can help them believe that their future can be different. 🤍

Df7TnBcEQ7E.caption:
Closed-Door Interview Look 🇯🇵✨

Sayuki is in her closed-door interview right now, proudly representing Japan. Sending her all our love and support🤍

Designed for the Miss Universe interview, this look expresses quiet confidence and intellect, inner strength, and the determination to take flight on the world stage.

A sharp white vest paired with black trousers creates a poised silhouette.

The long cape flowing from the shoulders features cranes reminiscent of Japanese ink paintings and a golden circle. Elegant and composed at rest, the design brings the cranes to life in movement, as though they are spreading their wings.

Inspired by the Japanese appreciation for space and the fluidity of brushstrokes, this creation embodies a woman who is thoughtful and composed, strong at her core, and ready to spread her wings to the world.

たった今、さゆきが日本代表としてクローズドドア・インタビューに挑んでいます🇯🇵
皆さま、応援よろしくお願いいたします🤍

白を基調としたシャープなジレスタイルに黒のパンツを合わせ、凛とした佇まいに。

そんな姿を一着の中に形にしました。

DcvM28fv9d3.caption:
Miss Universe Japan 2026 日本代表 伊藤さゆきと、ナショナルディレクター 美馬寛子が、内閣総理大臣 高市早苗様を表敬訪問いたしました。

日本初の女性総理大臣である高市総理を表敬訪問させていただくという、大変貴重な機会となりました。

懇談では、世界大会への出場を前に温かい激励のお言葉をいただくとともに、日本の魅力を世界へ発信していくことについて、そして「女性として」という枠にとらわれず、一人の人間、一人のリーダーとしてどうあるべきか、高市総理が考えるリーダー像についてもお話を伺うことができ、多くの学びと気づきをいただきました。

今回の表敬訪問にあたりご尽力いただきました、厚生労働副大臣 仁木博文様をはじめ、関係者の皆様に心より御礼申し上げます。

今回いただいた貴重なお言葉を胸に、伊藤さゆきの世界大会への挑戦とともに、これからも一人ひとりが自らの力で未来を切り拓き、社会に前向きな変化をもたらすリーダーへと成長していけるよう、その歩みを支えてまいります。

皆さま、引き続き温かい応援をよろしくお願いいたします。

Today, these lessons inspire her to serve her community, empower young people, and use her voice to create positive change. Her story is a reminder that difficult beginnings do not define a person’s future; they can become the foundation of a life dedicated to making a difference.

DfbRhLagrXc.caption:
The Grand Raid 

The Grand Raid Reunion race invites us to reflect on the way we experience a sporting event: do we run simply for the sake of running, or also to appreciate the magnificent nature that surrounds us? 

From October 15 to 18, approximately 6,200 runners made their way along the island's trails. But how can we preserve biodiversity during such a major sporting event?

At the Departmental Council of Reunion's stand, I interviewed two students who explained the differences between endemic, native, and exotic plants, as well as the “10 Commandments” to follow on the trails.

Thanks to Mael and Brandon, students specializing in Physical Education and Sports at Lycée Amiral Pierre Bouvet in Saint-Benoît, visitors could also take part in various activities focused on Réunion Island's plants.

Running is important, but so is respecting what makes our island unique.

DfTcOf6EvvD.caption:
It breaks my heart to see our mangroves burn; it is watching our very future erode before our eyes. 

The Alakiri fire  in Okrika , Rivers State. Nigeria, is a cry for help. A cry of pain. Our mangroves do so much more than hold our coastline in place; they absorb carbon, shelter marine life, and support the families and livelihoods across our communities. 

It deeply saddens me to witness them consumed by flames and toxic crude, yet we cannot turn away.

Miss Earth is not always about glamour; it’s about advocacy. In line with our theme, “Love in Action", Miss Earth transcends beauty and pageantry by inspiring meaningful action through environmental protection, sustainable education, community outreach, and climate change advocacy.

It means standing in the gap when our land is bleeding and using our platform to fight for real change.

This tragedy is happening now, in real time, and our environment needs us to turn empathy into impact. Join us in standing together for immediate restoration and long-term protection of our precious wetlands. 

Our ecosystems deserve our care, and our people deserve a safe, sustainable home.

Mercy Suoyo | Miss Earth Nigeria 2026

De8YE09ksm3.caption:
Earth Day in Action for a Cleaner Coast

A few days before Earth Day, we chose to do something rather than simply talk about it.

At Foz do Arelho, I joined a large community beach and lagoon clean-up that brought together around 100 people. Together, we removed approximately 548 kg of waste from the area, waste that could otherwise have remained in or reached the lagoon and the ocean.

Beyond the numbers, this activity helped me understand what happens to the waste we leave behind. Plastic does not simply disappear. It can fragment into smaller particles, enter aquatic ecosystems, affect marine life and eventually become part of the food chain.

That made me look differently at something as simple as a piece of plastic left on the sand. What we leave behind has a journey, and its impact can continue long after we walk away.

Foz do Arelho is part of the place I call home. Caring for it means more than keeping a beach clean, it means protecting the lagoon, the ocean, the biodiversity they support and, ultimately, ourselves.

As Miss Earth Portugal 2026, I want to be part of environmental action that I can experience and understand firsthand. And this day showed me the true power of collective action, around 100 people, approximately 548 kg of waste removed, and one ecosystem left cleaner than we found it.

Earth Day may come once a year. Our responsibility does not.

Dex3IZ3CNyH.caption:
The Water Cycle in Action

On World Water Day, I visited the Salinas de Rio Maior to explore a remarkable example of how the water cycle connects nature, geology and our everyday lives.

Here, rainwater infiltrates the ground and travels through layers of rock, reaching underground deposits of rock salt that naturally make the water saline. At the surface, sun, wind and evaporation gradually leave behind salt crystals, while the water returns to its natural cycle, a process that has supported salt production here for centuries.

Something as familiar as the salt on our table is therefore the result of an extraordinary natural journey, connecting water, geology, natural resources and human tradition.

As Miss Earth Portugal 2026, I believe protecting water also begins with understanding the processes it makes possible and recognizing how deeply our lives depend on them.

From rain, through the Earth, to salt, every drop is part of a much bigger story.

Denxss0CMui.caption:
Change does not always begin with a big action. Sometimes, it begins with a conversation.

Through my partnership with the Oeste UNESCO Global Geopark and the Rotary Clubs of Caldas da Rainha, I had the opportunity to take EndPlasticSoup directly into local schools, speaking with students about plastic pollution and the impact of our everyday choices.

EndPlasticSoup is a global Rotary environmental initiative working to end plastic pollution in our waters, soil and air by 2050. Its approach connects awareness, action and alliances, educating communities, encouraging practical change and bringing organizations together to create greater impact.

In the classroom, we explored the journey of plastic from our homes, through rivers, and ultimately into the ocean, helping students understand not only where pollution comes from but also how their choices can help prevent it.

For me, this was one of the most meaningful parts of the initiative, creating dialogue with younger generations, answering their questions, and giving them the knowledge and tools to become part of the solution.

As Miss Earth Portugal 2026, I believe environmental action must also begin with education. Taking this message into schools allowed me to turn awareness into something that can remain beyond that moment, knowledge that influences choices, and choices that create change.

Because ending plastic pollution will not happen through one action alone. It will be built school by school, river by river, coast

DejRMAODiHp.caption:
Does anyone else love desserts like cake or cookies? Today I want to introduce another way we can care for our Earth. I've always loved desserts—but recently I started discovering vegan desserts, which let me enjoy something I love while also being kinder to the planet. That’s why I want to introduce a well-known vegan dessert café in Korea, Plant Bakery Seoul plantbakeryseoul 🍰

Let me share why vegan desserts and bakeries make such a positive impact on our Earth 

🌾Plant-Based Baking, Lighter on the Earth
Traditional baking relies heavily on dairy, eggs, and butter — ingredients tied to animal agriculture, one of the biggest contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. Vegan bakeries replace these with plant-based alternatives, significantly reducing their environmental footprint.

💧Saving Water, One Bake at a Time
Producing dairy and eggs requires enormous amounts of water. By using plant-based ingredients like oat milk, almond butter, and flax eggs, vegan desserts help conserve one of our Earth‘s most precious resources.

🐄Reducing the Impact of Animal Agriculture
Choosing vegan desserts means choosing not to support industrial animal farming — a major source of deforestation, methane emissions, and land degradation. Every bite becomes a small but meaningful act of care for the Earth.

♻Mindful, Sustainable Ingredients
Many vegan bakeries, like Plant Bakery Seoul, focus on natural, sustainably sourced ingredients — supporting a food culture that's better for both our bodies

DeYijN3DXo2.caption:
Underwater Lagoon – A Cocoon of Biodiversity

As part of my role as Miss Earth Portugal 2026, I had the privilege of attending the opening of the photographic exhibition “Lagoa Subaquática – Um Casulo de Biodiversidade” (“Underwater Lagoon – A Cocoon of Biodiversity”) in Foz do Arelho, an environmental education initiative promoted by the Municipality of Caldas da Rainha.

Through 20 underwater photographs, the exhibition reveals a reality that often remains hidden beneath the waters of Óbidos Lagoon: an ecosystem rich in biodiversity, where seagrass meadows play an essential role in the reproduction, feeding, and development of different species of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs.

As a partner of the Caldas da Rainha Environmental Department, participating in this eco-activity allowed me to gain a closer understanding of the biodiversity of a territory that I also represent, while contributing to raising awareness within the community about the importance of its conservation.

Because protecting nature also begins with knowing it. And bringing to light what exists beneath the surface is a way of bringing people closer to nature and showing them the value of what we have right here, so close to us.

Dfz8pYmNcT-.caption:
Miss World Joheirry Mola visited The People’s Theatre (thepeoplestheatrenyc) in Inwood, New York City, where she was welcomed by Mino Lora, the theatre’s Dominican-born co-founder and executive artistic director, and New York City Council Member Carmen De La Rosa. Carmen moved from the Dominican Republic to New York as a child and grew up in Inwood, one of the neighborhoods she now represents in District 10.

Joheirry toured the Centro Cultural Inmigrante, the theatre’s first permanent home, which opened in September 2026. The center brings performances, rehearsal studios, and arts education together under one roof. It gives immigrant artists a place to develop and present new work and offers young people in Inwood and neighboring Washington Heights the chance to tell their own stories through theatre.

After the tour, Joheirry joined Mino and Carmen for a conversation with guests and members of the press. During the Q&A, a young woman told Joheirry she had been bullied for being of Dominican descent. What would she do in her place?

Joheirry encouraged her to be proud of her roots and of where her family came from, wherever she might find herself. No country is perfect, she said, and every country has something special to share with the world. She encouraged the young woman to speak about being Dominican with pride, even when someone tried to use it to hurt her. 

Thank you to Mino, Carmen, and The People’s Theatre for welcoming Miss World and making room for such an honest

Nearly 400 students gave Miss World Joheirry Mola a superstar welcome when she visited P.S. 132 Juan Pablo Duarte in New York this week. But once she sat down between the two students chosen to interview her, the questions were all about school. One of them put her on the spot. What was her least favorite subject?

Mola told the children she loved social studies, especially history, and admitted that she sometimes struggled with math. Her young interviewers had a follow-up. What did she do about it?

She told them that when she got home from school, she spent more time studying math than her other subjects. It took extra work to earn the grades she wanted, and she encouraged the children to do the same when they found a subject difficult. They could have their favorites, she said, and still give themselves a chance to learn something in every class.

Mola also encouraged the students to stay true to themselves, stay focused on their goals, and respect their parents and teachers. After the conversation, the children formed a long line for autographs. She signed nearly 400 photos, making time for each child and posing with those who asked for a picture.

A teacher herself, Mola has made education a priority during her reign. Through Voices of Tomorrow, her Beauty With a Purpose project, she helps children and teenagers in underserved communities learn English and gain the confidence to speak it. De54U7motXd.caption:
Today is October 25, that special date when the World comes together to celebrate JEM’s birthday.

Julia Morley CBE is a remarkable woman whose compassion has helped generations of young women discover their potential and use their talents to make a difference. Through Beauty With a Purpose, she created a platform that turns concern for others into action, bringing care, opportunity, and hope to people in need around the world.

In 2022, Queen Elizabeth II recognized her charitable and voluntary service to disadvantaged people in the United Kingdom and abroad by appointing her a Commander of the Order of the British Empire, the honor represented by the letters CBE.

Those who know Julia understand how deeply she cares for children. She believes no child should go hungry or grow up without protection, love, and the encouragement to become everything they dream of being. That belief is at the heart of her life’s work.

For the women who join Miss World, JEM is also a source of strength and reassurance. She cares for them as she would her own daughters, shares in their joys, and celebrates their achievements and important steps long after their time on the Miss World stage.

Today, we celebrate her life, her generous heart, her humor, and the countless lives she has touched. We also celebrate the woman we are so fortunate to know and love.

Happy Birthday, dear JEM. Much love from your Miss World family all around the globe!

On October 2, while traveling from Santo Domingo to Punta Cana, Miss World Joheirry Mola stopped in La Romana to visit Fundación Niños y Niñas de Cristo, a place she already knew and held close to her heart.

Supported by goyafoods and goya_gives, the foundation provides a safe, loving home for vulnerable children and adolescents, including those who have experienced abandonment or abuse. Its work combines education, nutritious meals, healthcare, recreation, and practical skills to help them build a brighter future.

Having visited several times before, Joheirry returned to a special welcome filled with applause and familiar faces. She also met one of the home’s youngest residents, one-month-old Stephen, and her friend David, who was anxiously waiting for her.

With her warm hugs, generous smiles, and natural connection with children, Miss World quickly made everyone feel at ease. She reminded them that she was still the same Joheirry who had come to visit before, and that it was time to have fun.

Soon, everyone headed outside to the courtyard, where music, games, and laughter turned the visit into a joyful afternoon together.

When Julia Morley CBE saw the images, she commented: “I am so proud of Joheirry! This is Beauty With a Purpose and what Miss World is all about”.

Dd_8WcOpaUF.caption:
In Santiago de los Caballeros, Miss World Joheirry Mola immersed herself in Dominican culture, history, art, and identity, visiting two cultural centers before ending her day at one of the city’s most recognizable landmarks.

Her visit started at Centro Cultural Eduardo León Jimenes (centroleonrd), where art, history, and exhibitions invite visitors to discover the diversity of Dominican identity and the traditions that have shaped the nation.

At Centro Cultural Banreservas (centroculturalbr), a space dedicated to preserving cultural heritage and supporting artistic talent, she visited “Orgánico y Desenfadado,” a retrospective of Dominican artist Persio Checo. His paintings and sculptures draw on surrealism, nature, and the sea, creating an imaginative world of color and organic forms. Joheirry was particularly impressed by the beauty of his work, another expression of the Dominican creativity she is proud to share with the world.

Although this was not her first visit to Santiago, the city continues to impress her. For Joheirry, returning as Miss World was an opportunity to share her pride in her country and introduce a global audience to its Dominican and Latin American roots.

The day concluded at the Monumento a los Héroes de la Restauración, which honors those who fought to restore Dominican independence during the War of Restoration, from 1863 to 1865.

DdanOZ7p9_X.caption:
On their final day of official activities in Vietnam, Miss World 2026 Joheirry Mola, First Runner-Up Elisabeth Reynés and Second Runner-Up Taanusiya Chetty discovered three very different sides of Nha Trang: its extraordinary island environment, marine heritage and centuries-old culture.

The day began with a journey by sea to Hòn Nội, known as Yến Island, one of Khánh Hòa’s swiftlet islands. During several hours on the island, the Top 3 explored its coastal landscape and learned about the traditional bird’s nest industry, an important part of Khánh Hòa’s cultural and economic heritage.

Their visit included Hòn Sam swiftlet cave, where they discovered more about the birds, their nesting environment and the traditional methods associated with harvesting the highly prized edible nests. They also took part in an incense-offering ceremony at the temple honoring the ancestral figure of Khánh Hòa’s bird’s nest profession. 

Surrounded by turquoise water, rocky cliffs and spectacular views, the visit combined discovery with a little adventure. After approximately 90 minutes traveling by sea to reach the island, the Top 3 spent the morning exploring, filming and enjoying a side of Khánh Hòa that few international visitors have the opportunity to experience. They also shared lunch on the island before making the journey back to Nha Trang.

The afternoon continued at the Institute of Oceanography, where they discovered more about Vietnam’s marine life, biodiversity and scientific rese

DdYxnMTJXtD.caption:
The Top 3 Miss World 2026 joined a special early celebration of Tết Trung Thu, Vietnam’s traditional Mid-Autumn Festival, at the Khánh Hòa Provincial Children’s Cultural Palace in Nha Trang.

Known in Vietnam as the Children’s Festival, Tết Trung Thu is one of the country’s most cherished traditions, bringing families and communities together through colorful lanterns, music, lion and dragon dances, mooncakes and celebrations dedicated especially to children. 

Miss World 2026 Joheirry Mola, First Runner-Up Elisabeth Reynes Alabern and Second Runner-Up Taanusiya Veerapandian enjoyed the festivities alongside the children, joining the celebrations and sharing a joyful evening filled with performances and traditional Mid-Autumn activities.

Joheirry also addressed the children and guests, sharing a few words on behalf of the Top 3 before the three joined the gift presentation.

A total of 1,500 gifts were prepared for children across Khánh Hòa. Five hundred were presented directly during the celebration, while another 1,000 were sent to children at shelters, care facilities and social protection centers across the northern part of the province. 

The occasion also brought the Top 3 back to a familiar place. During the 75th Anniversary Miss World Festival, the Khánh Hòa Children’s Cultural Palace welcomed the National Ambassadors for some of the competition’s memorable events, including the Head-to-Head Challenge and Talent Competition.

Dc0TngspNxh.caption:
The Multimedia Final Challenge took place earlier today, September 3, introducing a completely new and original format to the competition.

The four continental winners were welcomed by reigning Mr World Danny Mejía, who explained the challenge before inviting them into a room where six very special guests were waiting:

Miss World 2025, Opal Suchata Chuangsri
Miss World 2024, Krystyna Pyszková
Miss World 2022, Karolina Bielawska
Miss World 2018, Vanessa Ponce de León
Miss World 2016, Stephanie Del Valle
Miss World 1988, Linda Pétursdóttir
Miss World 1975, Wilnelia Merced Forsyth

Each Miss World was seated at a different station, and the finalists had four minutes with each of them. They were free to ask any questions they wished and capture photos, selfies and videos. Once time was called, they moved on to the next station, continuing until each finalist had spoken with all six titleholders.

With five additional minutes allowed for any final shots or adjustments, the finalists are now using the material they collected to create a two-minute video celebrating Miss World’s 75-year history through the stories and experiences shared by these remarkable women.

The completed videos must be submitted by 11:59 PM tonight. One of the four finalists will be named the overall Multimedia Award winner during the Miss World Final on September 5 and will earn a fast-track place in the Top 20.

The 4 Multimedia Challenge Continental Winners are audreyhowentsaioff 🇬🇫, adahmushibi 🇿🇲, juli

Dczx_GyJhxt.caption:
The Multimedia Final Challenge took place this morning, September 3, introducing a completely new and original format to the competition.

The four continental winners were welcomed by reigning Mr World Danny Mejía, who explained the challenge before inviting them into a room where six very special guests were waiting:

Miss World 2025, Opal Suchata Chuangsri
Miss World 2024, Krystyna Pyszková
Miss World 2022, Karolina Bielawska
Miss World 2018, Vanessa Ponce de León
Miss World 2016, Stephanie Del Valle
Miss World 1975, Wilnelia Merced Forsyth

Each Miss World was seated at a different station, and the finalists had four minutes with each of them. They were free to ask any questions they wished and capture photos, selfies and videos. Once time was called, they moved on to the next station, continuing until each finalist had spoken with all six titleholders.

With five additional minutes allowed for any final shots or adjustments, the finalists are now using the material they collected to create a two-minute video celebrating Miss World’s 75-year history through the stories and experiences shared by these remarkable women.

The completed videos must be submitted by 11:59 PM tonight. One of the four finalists will be named the overall Multimedia Award winner during the Miss World Final on September 5 and will earn a fast-track place in the Top 20.

The 4 Multimedia Challenge Continental Winners are audreyhowentsaioff 🇬🇫, adahmushibi 🇿🇲, juliaofgermany 🇩🇪, and deybianca 🇮🇩.

DcyiTNzOfGx.caption:
On September 2, all 111 Miss World national ambassadors took to the spectacular stage in Nha Trang to showcase their national costumes and traditional dances in a vibrant celebration of culture, heritage and unity.

Held as Vietnam celebrated the 81st anniversary of its independence, “Hello Vietnam, Hello World” brought nations together through color, music and movement. Just three days before the Miss World Final and the celebration of Miss World’s 75-year history, each national ambassador proudly shared the traditions and spirit of her homeland.

Among those in attendance were Julia Morley CBE, President and Chairwoman of the Miss World Organization; representatives of the Sen Vàng host committee; and Miss World titleholders Opal Suchata Chuangsri, Miss World titleholders Krystyna Pyszková, Karolina Bielawska, Vanessa Ponce de León, Linda Pétursdóttir and Lady Wilnelia Merced Forsyth. National directors from more than 100 countries, sponsors, and the families and friends of the national ambassadors also joined the celebration.

Hosted by reigning Mr World Danny Mejía and the 66th Miss World, Stephanie del Valle, the unforgettable event welcomed an audience of approximately 10,000 people.

It was truly a night to remember!

🌐 missgrandinternational.com
💰 1 Vote = THB 35

The competition features 𝟑 𝐕𝐎𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐑𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃𝐒, giving contestants multiple opportunities to qualify automatically for the Miss Grand International 2026 Grand Final.

🔹 𝐑𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃 𝟏 — 𝐓𝐎𝐏 𝟐𝟎
- Uses accumulated votes since voting first opened.
- Closes at 7:00 PM (GMT+7) on Grand Final night.
- The contestant with the highest votes automatically enters the TOP 20.
- Scores reset to ZERO for Round 2.

🔹 𝐑𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃 𝟐 — 𝐓𝐎𝐏 𝟏𝟎
- Opens after the TOP 20 announcement and closes after the Swimsuit Competition.
- ALL contestants remain eligible, including those who did not advance to the TOP 20.
- The contestant with the highest votes automatically enters the TOP 10.
- Scores reset to ZERO for Round 3.

🔹 𝐑𝐎𝐔𝐍𝐃 𝟑 — 𝐓𝐎𝐏 𝟓
- Opens after the TOP 10 announcement and closes after the Question & Answer round.
- ALL contestants remain eligible, including those who did not advance to the TOP 10.
- The contestant with the highest votes automatically enters the TOP 5, wins 𝐌𝐈𝐒𝐒 𝐏𝐎𝐏𝐔𝐋𝐀𝐑 𝐕𝐎𝐓𝐄, and is guaranteed at least 4th Runner-Up.

⚠️ 𝐈𝐌𝐏𝐎𝐑𝐓𝐀𝐍𝐓 𝐍𝐎𝐓𝐄𝐒
- Scores reset to ZERO at the start of Rounds 2 and 3. Previous votes do not carry over.

- Contestants eliminated from the main competition can still win Miss Popular Vote.

- The winner of this title is determined solely by votes received in Round 3.

Every vote counts! Support your favorite at missgrandinternational.com 🔥

Représenter la France à Miss Universe serait un immense honneur pour moi, d’autant plus que je pourrais défendre aux côtés de planfrance une cause qui me tient énormément à cœur : l’éducation et l’indépendance des jeunes filles.

DeKJxpzNxm3.caption:
On m’a souvent dit qu’il fallait choisir. Définir une voie et s’y tenir.
Moi, j’ai tout choisi.

J’ai grandi entre les études et le mannequinat, en construisant mon parcours en finance tout en voyageant et en travaillant à travers le monde. De Madrid à Londres, en passant par les États-Unis, j’ai appris très tôt à m’adapter, à travailler et à aller au bout de mes ambitions.

Avec le recul, je réalise que toutes ces expériences m’ont préparée à ce moment. Elles m’ont appris à me dépasser, à croire en mes choix et surtout à ne jamais me laisser enfermer dans une seule voie.

Aujourd’hui, je fais partie du Top 3 de missuniversefr . 
Être si proche de représenter la France à Miss Univers est une immense fierté. Si j’ai cette chance, je suis prête à me dépasser encore plus et à tout donner pour porter la France le plus loin possible.

Bravo à toutes les candidates avec qui j’ai partagé cette aventure, et merci au comité pour sa confiance et toutes ces belles rencontres.

Et surtout, merci à vous pour vos messages, votre bienveillance et votre soutien. Plus que jamais, j’ai besoin de vous à mes côtés pour cette dernière étape. ❤️

Je suis arrivée jusqu’ici en restant fidèle à celle que je suis. Maintenant, je compte bien aller jusqu’au bout. 🇫🇷✨

De2DGAwgHEt.caption:
👑🇲🇩 MISS UNIVERSE MOLDOVA 2026 - Dorina Darii 🇲🇩👑

Cu mare bucurie și mândrie, vă prezentăm oficial noua MISS UNIVERSE MOLDOVA!

În urma unui proces de selecție la care s-au înscris aproape 100 de candidate, fiecare cu propria poveste, personalitate, ambiții și visuri, organizația Miss Universe Moldova a ales astăzi, în mod oficial, tânăra care va avea onoarea și responsabilitatea de a reprezenta Republica Moldova pe una dintre cele mai prestigioase scene internaționale.

✨ DORINA DARII va reprezenta oficial Moldova în MISS UNIVERSE 2026 in Puerto Rico, în perioada 8-25 noiembrie 👑🇲🇩

Frumusețea, eleganța, inteligența, încrederea în sine și personalitatea ei au făcut-o să se remarce în timpul selecției și i-au adus acest titlu atât de râvnit.

În luna noiembrie, Dorina va purta cu mândrie numele și drapelul Republicii Moldova la MISS UNIVERSE 2026, alături de reprezentante din aproximativ 130 de țări. 🌎

Vrem să le mulțumim din suflet tuturor candidatelor care au participat la selecție. Vă mulțumim pentru încredere, curaj, entuziasm și pentru dorința de a reprezenta Moldova. Fiecare dintre voi a avut un rol important în această poveste și merită toată aprecierea noastră!
Așteptăm în continuare înscrierile voastre prin DM pe Instagram, pentru ediția din 2027.

Astăzi începe un nou capitol, plin de emoții, provocări și oportunități extraordinare.

🇲🇩 O NOUĂ REGINĂ. O NOUĂ POVESTE. O ȚARĂ ÎNTREAGĂ DE REPREZENTAT.🇲🇩

Dddm4N4ukvm.caption:
From being bullied to becoming a voice of encouragement. 

During her visit to a primary school in Kenya, Miss Universe Netherlands opened her heart and shared a deeply personal part of her story. She spoke to the children about being bullied when she was younger, and about learning to see her own worth despite the words and actions of others.

Her message was simple, but powerful: you are good enough exactly as you are. 

She encouraged the children to believe in themselves, embrace what makes them unique, and always choose kindness because the way we treat one another can leave a lasting impact.

This is what using a platform with purpose looks like. With openness, compassion and a pure heart, Miss Universe Netherlands turns her own experiences into strength for others. If her story can make even one child feel seen, valued and a little more confident, then sharing it is worth everything. ❤️

Be kind. Be proud of who you are. And never let anyone make you feel like you are less than enough.

Df5ApVho1eV.caption:
La Organización Señorita Panamá presenta «Diosa Panamá – El oro verde» Traje nacional de Gabriela Lineth González, Miss Universe Panamá 2026, creado por el diseñador panameño César Pinilla.

César Pinilla concibió este diseño para la Gala Viva Panamá de Miss Universe Panamá 2026, donde obtuvo el primer lugar con su propuesta original en tonos dorados. Al adaptar el traje a las medidas de Gabriela, César Anel Rodríguez, presidente de la Organización Señorita Panamá, solicitó una versión a todo color para resaltar la riqueza visual de la propuesta y realzar el tono de piel de nuestra representante.

«Diosa Panamá – El oro verde» rinde homenaje a la biodiversidad panameña. Un body de transparencias bordado con cristales y pedrería en tonos verde esmeralda evoca la vegetación de nuestras selvas. Grandes hojas tropicales enmarcan la silueta, mientras dos guacamayas rojas de alas desplegadas se posan sobre los hombros. Las mariposas tropicales evocan la libertad y la transformación, y una cascada de heliconias aporta color y movimiento desde la cintura. Un tocado inspirado en hojas y ramas corona el conjunto y transforma a Gabriela en una diosa de la naturaleza panameña.

Con esta creación, Gabriela González lleva al escenario de Miss Universo un homenaje a la riqueza natural de Panamá.

Como Directores Nacionales, tenemos la responsabilidad de proteger y fortalecer una organización que durante décadas ha construido un legado de alcance mundial, actuando con respeto, responsabilidad y compromiso con la institución que representamos en nuestros respectivos países.

Esta declaración refleja la posición compartida por la mayoría de los Directores Nacionales de Miss Universe, quienes permanecemos unidos en defensa de la estabilidad, integridad y continuidad de la Organización.

Dc3rKO0OIiA.caption:
GALA VIVA PANAMÁ | COMITÉ DE SELECCIÓN

La Gala Viva Panamá representa una de las noches más importantes en el camino hacia la corona. Como parte de la competencia preliminar de Miss Universe Panamá 2026, nuestras 27 candidatas tendrán la oportunidad de demostrar su preparación, proyección y seguridad, además de celebrar nuestra identidad a través de la competencia de Mejor Traje Típico. 👑✨

Presentamos a Eric “Nene” Polo, Licenciado en Folklore Superior. 

Oriundo de la ciudad de Las Tablas, es Licenciado en Folklore Superior, con una destacada trayectoria dedicada a la investigación, preservación y promoción de las tradiciones y expresiones culturales de Panamá.

Su labor lo ha llevado a recorrer diferentes rincones del país, con especial énfasis en el estudio y conocimiento de las indumentarias tradicionales panameñas, contribuyendo a preservar y exaltar nuestra identidad cultural.

Cuenta además con amplia experiencia como asesor de reinas y festividades nacionales, aportando sus conocimientos y experiencia al fortalecimiento de nuestras tradiciones y manifestaciones folklóricas.

Nos llena de orgullo presentar a Carla-Mari Schellink, Directora de Clínicas & Spa Médico Oficial de Miss Universe Panamá 2026 y miembro de nuestro exclusivo Bureau de Expertos.

Fundadora y Directora de Impilo Plastic Surgery & Medical Spa e Impilo Organics, Carla-Mari cuenta con más de 15 años de experiencia internacional en clínicas de cirugía plástica y spas médicos, habiendo desarrollado su carrera en ciudades como Londres, Miami, Dubai y Abu Dhabi antes de establecerse en Panamá.

DcryJwjRq5T.caption:
Il y a encore tellement de choses que vous ne savez pas sur moi.

2026 restera sans doute l’une des années les plus marquantes de ma vie. Celle où j’ai décidé d’affronter mes peurs, de sortir de ma zone de confort et, surtout, d’oser. Professionnellement comme personnellement.

Cette année, j’ai réussi à dépasser certaines peurs que je pensais parfois plus fortes que moi. Des expériences, des épreuves et des victoires que j’aurai à cœur de vous raconter, notamment en vidéo, parce que je suis convaincue que nos histoires peuvent parfois donner à quelqu’un d’autre la force d’écrire la sienne différemment.

Moi aussi, j’ai été inspirée par des femmes et des hommes qui ont eu le courage d’être transparents, de parler de leurs doutes, de leurs faiblesses, de leurs peurs… mais aussi du chemin parcouru pour les dépasser.

Aujourd’hui, à mon tour, j’ai envie de partager davantage avec vous. Pas seulement mes réussites, mais aussi le chemin qui se cache derrière elles.

C’est aussi le message que je souhaite porter durant cette aventure : nos vulnérabilités ne nous rendent pas moins forts. Partagées avec sincérité, elles peuvent devenir une force capable d’en inspirer d’autres.

J’ai été inspirée.
À mon tour, j’espère pouvoir inspirer.

Merci d’être là. 🤍

Df7wpk6jK1N.caption:
For one of the most personal moments of my journey, I wanted to wear something that felt like home.

Designed by Anthony Ramirez, this suit was made from custom Inabel fabric woven in my hometown of La Union, bringing together traditional Filipino craftsmanship and contemporary tailoring. The structured, off-shoulder silhouette features personalized mother-of-pearl seashell buttons accented with Swarovski gold pearls, along with a custom starfish detail that makes the piece even more special to me.

The color red carries a meaning of its own. On the Philippine flag, it represents courage, bravery, and patriotism — values I carry with me as I represent my country on this journey.

Every little detail is also a reflection of my connection to the sea. The ocean has always held a special place in my heart, not only because of where I come from, but because protecting it is one of the causes I deeply care about.

For my closed-door interview, I wanted to wear something that represented more than just my personal style. Something that carried my roots, my purpose, and the things I believe in.

A piece of home, and a reminder of what I’m here for. 🇵🇭

Df7SzkKIzTv.caption:
What does it mean to represent a nation? And what responsibility comes with being given that platform?

In my TEDxManila talk, “The Politics of Pretty: The Role of Pageantry in Nation Building,” I explore how pageants have shaped our national imagination, influenced ideas of beauty and representation, and become part of how we see ourselves as a country.

I also reflect on a tension I carry as an activist and academic who critiques the very institution I now participate in. I believe we can acknowledge these contradictions while still asking difficult questions and working toward meaningful change.

Because pageantry should be about more than who gets the crown. It should also challenge us to imagine who gets represented, whose voices are heard, and what kind of future we want to build.

I invite you to watch and engage with the full talk.

Today, I carry these same convictions into my Closed-Door Interview at Miss Universe. 🇵🇭

The greatest honor and responsibility is to wear the Philippines across my heart.

DfhjXOvllUj.caption:
7,641 islands, one nation. 

In the Philippines, the oceans connect rather than divide us. Across the islands, the sea facilitates movement, shared language and customs, connection through the flow of migration and movement. 

Just as an archipelago is a whole unit comprised of islands connected by the sea, the concept of pakikipagkapwa is the recognition of shared humanity, connection, and the understanding that the the other person is never truly the other. It is the belief that we share the same joys, sorrows, hopes, and aspirations because our identity is deeply interconnected. 

Perhaps that is why, in a country made up of thousands of islands, no community stands alone. To represent the Philippines is to know that I am never alone. 

Mabuhay, Philippines 🤍🌊💫

As I raise our flag on the international stage here in Puerto Rico, I look forward to exploring the stunning Sierra de Luquillo mountain range in El Yunque National Forest.

DewVO98kyWz.caption:
Protecting our oceans isn’t just about preserving nature, it also uplifts communities, guards our homes, and secures our very way of life. 🐢🌊 

In the Philippines, the ocean economy accounted for 1.08 trillion PHP in 2025. Beyond numbers, those are millions of families nourished from fishing, communities across the archipelago dependent on tourism, and countless individuals who sustain themselves on the seas. 

I am honored to bring my work with Project CURMA to the Miss Universe stage because their holistic conservation approach recognizes how our changing climate is deeply tied to the livelihoods of millions in coastal communities. Their community-led projects and ridge-to-reef approach serves as a model for other environmental protection efforts across the country. 

Hopefully, their efforts can echo across the Universe and be a reminder that a small ripple in one community can become an unstoppable tidal wave for change ✨

My Voice for Change video is now re-uploaded on the Miss Universe YT page! Please consider viewing, liking, and sharing to support the incredible work of Project CURMA: https://youtu.be/yLrJ-0gB5Pw?si=jQA2H2PhBzITYKNG

DeeR4V-k0YL.caption:
Soft smiles against soaring concrete arches 🌺

The Ruins are one of the Philippines’ architectural wonders, solidly built with high-grade concrete and railroad metal reinforcements. The over-100 year estate was built as an act of love to symbolize sugar baron Don Mariano’s eternal commitment to his late wife, Maria Braga Lacson. 

During the advent of WWII, Filipino guerrilla forces made the practical yet difficult decision to burn the estate for three days to prevent advancing Japanese forces from procuring the mansion as a military command center. 

Despite extensive damage from the fire, the strong concrete frame and pillars still stand as a reminder that love, dedication, and beauty still persevere, even through the most challenging circumstances 🤍

Para sa komunidad. Para sa kalikasan. Para sa aking bansa. 🇵🇭

With less than a month left till I depart for Miss Universe in San Juan, Puerto Rico, I stand with a heart full of gratitude and pride. It is the honor of a lifetime to represent my beloved Philippines on the international stage. 

In my six months as Miss Universe Philippines, I have spent every day trying to live up to my promise of being a public servant for all. From working with climate vulnerable communities on our coasts, to mangrove reforestation and marine biodiversity conservation work, to uplifting migrant workers and their families, to advocating for equal protections for our LGBTIA+ brothers and sisters. 

To me, pageantry holds a responsibility far greater than crowns and sashes. It provides a platform to advocate for our world’s most underserved communities and the opportunity to envision the kind of future we deserve. 

As I step onto the Miss Universe stage, my greatest pride will be to carry the stories of my kabaybayan, and to promote a future where all voices are heard.

Our land, our resources, our environment, and the Filipino people hold far more value than developments that solely focus on shareholder profits and a frenzied AI market with no promises of longevity or sustainable development. What we do know is that data centers generate a heat island effect, warming our already changing climate and consume immense amounts of energy, water, and resources in our already overburdened communities.

We must recognize the heroic efforts of communities in Nueva Vizcaya and recognize that these struggles are intertwined.

DfSMcFrxZ4H.caption:
Beyond the Crown | Miss Universe Canada 🇨🇦

I have always believed that our beginnings are part of our story, but they should never define the limits of our future.

Having seen firsthand how education can change the course of a life, I founded LEAP Global Voices to help young people recognize their potential and create opportunities for their futures.

Rooted in UN Sustainable Development Goal 4: Quality Education, my work spans supporting girls’ education in Türkiye, providing school supplies to children in the Philippines, and leading workshops in Canadian classrooms, where students develop Dream Life Maps and write letters to their future selves.

I believe education is more than academic achievement. It gives people the independence to make choices, the confidence to pursue their ambitions, and the opportunity to build lives of dignity and purpose.

We may not all have the same opportunities, but we all have the ability to make a difference. My hope is that we use what we have, wherever we are, to create opportunities for someone else.

DdS8DYuAL9D.caption:
With so many new faces here, and as I prepare to represent Canada in Puerto Rico, I felt it was time to share more than an introduction. I wanted to share the story that shaped me.

I came to Canada from Türkiye as a little girl, raised by a single mother who taught me what resilience, sacrifice and starting over truly look like. We did not begin with much, but I grew up learning that your circumstances do not get to decide the size of your dreams. Education, opportunity and the freedom to choose a different future changed the course of our lives, and they became the foundation of the woman I am today.

That is why my journey to Miss Universe Canada has always been about more than a crown. I want to continue to connect meaningfully with communities, advocate for education and opportunity, and use this platform to remind others of the power of believing in themselves. To me, leadership means showing up with humility, authenticity and kindness, while helping people feel seen, valued and capable of more.

As I begin this next chapter on the road to Miss Universe, my greatest hope is to build something that reaches far beyond a crown. To create impact, open doors, connect communities, and remind others that where they begin does not determine where they are going.

A crown may give you a platform. Purpose is what gives it meaning. If any part of my story speaks to yours, I hope you’ll stay for the journey. There is so much more to come 🤍💫

Ontem deixei Cabo Verde com o coração cheio de sonhos. 
Vim para os Estados Unidos para continuar minha preparação para o Miss Universo, vivendo um daqueles momentos que, um dia, eu só imaginava.

I came to the United States to continue my Miss Universe preparation, living one of those moments I once could only imagine.
Being here, seeing New York, and experiencing all of this as Miss Universe Cabo Verde is a reminder that dreams really can come true.
May I never forget where I started and may you never stop believing in where you can go.

DdpM0BljLq3.caption:
Hoje tive o privilégio de conhecer as Nações Unidas em Cabo Verde e viver uma experiência que levarei para a vida.
Foi incrível conhecer mais sobre o trabalho, trocar ideias e conversar sobre os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS), que nos inspiram a construir um futuro mais justo, inclusivo e sustentável.
Poder compartilhar as minhas ideias e, ao mesmo tempo, ouvir diferentes perspectivas foi realmente especial.
Muito obrigada por essa experiência! 

Today, I had the privilege of visiting the United Nations in Cabo Verde and experiencing something I will carry with me for a lifetime. 
It was an incredible opportunity to learn more about the UN’s work, exchange ideas, and discuss the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which inspire us to build a more just, inclusive, and sustainable future.
Being able to share my ideas while also listening to different perspectives made this experience truly special.
Thank you for such a meaningful experience! 🤍

DcwIfZxMJzv.caption:
Antiga Ribeira Grande, hoje Cidade Velha, é o berço da história de Cabo Verde. Foi a primeira cidade do arquipélago e um importante ponto de encontro de diferentes povos e culturas. DfNxfhRCVYe.caption:
This is what it’s all about. 💕

I recently had the opportunity to visit a high school and speak with students about pageantry, perseverance, and my platform, Found in Translation.

Many of the students, like me, are children of immigrants. As they prepared for graduation and the next chapter of their lives, I encouraged them to keep dreaming without borders. 🌎✨

Usually, when I talk about borders, I’m referring to the geographical and cultural boundaries that can divide us. But this time, we talked about a different kind of border: the fear of failure.

The fear of trying something new. Of taking a different path. Of dreaming bigger than what seems possible.

Through Found in Translation, I use the A.R.T. of storytelling: Amplify Artists, Raise Awareness, and Transform Communities.

And this visit was especially close to my heart because it brought the T—Transform Communities—into practice.

A special thank-you to Ms. Jackson for welcoming me into your classroom and creating a space where young people are encouraged to learn, dream, and discover what's possible. 💕

By sharing our stories, we can encourage others to see new possibilities for their own.
Because sometimes, all it takes is one story to remind someone that their dreams are worth pursuing. ❤️

Avec amour,
Tatenda 💋

DfE_4GDiZmL.caption:
Because she flew, I can fly. 🪽🇹🇹🇭🇹🌎

In 1977, Janelle Commissiong of Trinidad and Tobago made history as the first Black woman to be crowned Miss Universe.

At a time when Eurocentric beauty standards dominated the world stage, her victory challenged the idea that beauty had to look a certain way.

She showed the world that Black women could BE the standard.

The standard of beauty. Of elegance. Of intelligence. Of grace.

When I first saw this photograph of Janelle wearing her hummingbird-inspired national costume, taken just days after her historic victory, the words immediately came to me:

Because she flew, I can fly.

Nearly 50 years later, I have the privilege of representing another Caribbean nation on that same stage.

My message? You don’t have to BE the world’s standard of beauty. Every woman has the power to DEFINE beauty for herself. 

Regardless of your shape, size, features, or how you wear your hair, you deserve to feel beautiful exactly as you are.

From one Caribbean woman to another, thank you, Janelle Commissiong, for breaking barriers and showing generations of women what was possible.

Because you flew, we can fly. ❤️

Tatenda 💋

De70s6uiQ5J.caption:
The truth about pageantry… 👑

1️⃣ **It amplifies who you already are.** 

The strengths AND the weaknesses. So know thyself.

2️⃣ **You’ll wear more hats than crowns.** 

One day you’re rubbing shoulders with dignitaries, the next you’re exploring a cave, and the next you’re visiting a school. Ambassador. Influencer. Educator. You’ll be them all and more—sometimes in the same day. Shapeshift, baby! 💃🏽

3️⃣ **The glitz and glam can be the smallest part of the job.** 

Community service, administration, transportation, interviews, and preparation take up more of my time than photoshoots and glam. Every reign is different. Romanticize all of it. ✨

4️⃣ **You’ll hear “no” more than you expect.** 

Not every sponsor will say yes, and not every opportunity will materialize. You’ll have to pivot gracefully, quickly, publicly—and probably in heels. Learn to make peace with rejection.

5️⃣ **You can’t please everyone.** 

Everyone will have an opinion about how you can improve. Some advice will help you grow; some won’t be right for you. Learn the difference, stay open to growth, and keep moving forward. A reign goes by fast.

Still here? 👀 Follow my journey to Miss Universe at tatendarameau and vote for Haiti through the link in my bio! 🇭🇹❤️

Avec amour,
Tatenda

Ddq9RFEEQMp.caption:
✨Marie Antoinette ✨

Backstage, as I tried on this look for the first time, I was told it was partly inspired by Marie Antoinette.

I smiled.

There was something powerful about the image: a Haitian woman walking a New York runway dressed like modern aristocracy. 

But the history makes the moment even more interesting. Fashion didn’t simply travel from Europe to the Caribbean. It traveled the other way, too. The robe à la créole—a style with roots in the French Caribbean—helped influence the dress that would become associated with Marie Antoinette herself.

Centuries later, I got to step onto a runway and reinterpret that history in my own way. 🇭🇹👑

Thank you Alexis Monsanto alexismonsanto for letting me tell a little piece of my story through yours. 🤍

DfOjP61EbAW.caption:
¡Rumbo a Puerto Rico! 🇵🇷🇭🇳

Hoy comienza una nueva aventura que recibo con muchísima ilusión, emoción y, sobre todo, gratitud. Partir desde Honduras llevando conmigo nuestra bandera es un orgullo que no se puede describir con palabras.

Cada viaje representa una oportunidad para aprender, crecer, conocer nuevas personas y, en esta ocasión, compartir un poquito de lo que somos como país: nuestra cultura, nuestra calidez, nuestras tradiciones y esa esencia tan especial que nos caracteriza como hondureños.

Me llevo el cariño de quienes me acompañan desde casa, el esfuerzo de todos los que hacen posible esta experiencia y la responsabilidad de representar a Honduras con autenticidad, elegancia y mucho corazón.

Gracias a cada persona que ha sido parte de este camino y que, de una u otra manera, me impulsa a seguir soñando en grande.

¡Honduras, esta aventura también es de ustedes! Nos vemos pronto, Puerto Rico ❤️🇭🇳

Dfx8pQtAKgC.caption:
Mis raíces me dieron identidad. Mi carácter me dio fuerza. Y mis sueños me enseñaron a volar. 🇲🇽

Vengo de una tierra donde se aprende a trabajar antes que a rendirse. Crecí creyendo que debía suavizar mi temperamento para encajar, hasta que entendí que no necesitaba cambiar quién soy, sino aprender a dirigir mi fuerza.

Hoy, desde Puerto Rico, cumpliendo el sueño de representar a México ante el universo, confirmo algo:

Nuestro origen no es un límite, nuestro carácter no es una condena y nuestra historia no determina nuestro destino.

No importa de dónde vengas, siempre puedes aprender, transformarte y llegar más lejos sin dejar de ser tú.

De Copalita para el universo. 🌎🇲🇽

Antes de salir a representar a México, tenía que volver a mi hogar. 🤍

Al lugar donde aprendí a creer, donde está mi familia, mi historia y las personas que me conocieron mucho antes de una banda o una corona.

Esta misa no fue para celebrar un título. Fue para dar gracias.

Gracias a Dios por el camino, a mi familia por sostenerme y a mi comunidad por recibirme con tanto amor.

Hoy entiendo que representar a México también significa llevar conmigo un pedacito del lugar que me vio crecer.

De Copalita para el mundo. 🇲🇽✨

🇵🇷 Puerto Rico, cada día estamos más cerca… 👑

DdW1378HMBn.caption:
Siempre soñé con llevar el nombre de México por el mundo. Hoy tengo el honor de hacerlo, y no hay orgullo más grande que representar mis raíces, mi historia y a mi país.

México, este sueño también es tuyo. 🇲🇽✨

Dc4CvHrFEGb.caption:
Después de días que todavía se sienten un poco irreales, entrevistas, viajes, cámaras y de intentar guardar en la memoria cada momento, volver y abrazar a mi familia se sintió como abrir una página conocida de mi historia.

Regresar se sintió como una celebración, como una forma muy bonita de decir: seguimos siendo los mismos de siempre, solo que ahora tenemos un sueño más que celebrar juntos.

DczopbyAJ_t.caption:
Si pudiera sentarme con la María de hace algunos años, creo que tendría tantas cosas que contarle. Le diría que siga trabajando, que se atreva, que disfrute más, que no tenga miedo de equivocarse y, sobre todo, que confíe en que cada etapa tiene algo que enseñarle.

Hoy entiendo que no todo lo que vivimos tiene sentido mientras está pasando. Hay momentos que duelen, planes que cambian y caminos que no entendemos, hasta que un día miramos hacia atrás y nos damos cuenta de todo lo que nos dejaron.

Le diría que los sueños se construyen en cada intento, en cada miedo que nos atrevemos a enfrentar, en cada decisión y, también, en cada persona que cree en nosotros cuando todavía estamos aprendiendo a creer en nosotros mismos.

Y si algo quiero llevar conmigo en esta nueva etapa es eso: no olvidar de dónde vengo y disfrutar profundamente hacia dónde voy.

Gracias a quienes han estado conmigo en el camino. Esto apenas comienza.

Dfvd_tOtZE9.caption: It was a day filled with powerful stories, inspiring women, courage, and so much love. I had the opportunity to meet some truly incredible women whose strength and resilience touched my heart. One woman in particular left a very special impression on me. She shared her personal journey, her family, and her experience with cancer. Listening to her story moved me deeply and reminded me of the incredible strength of the human spirit. I wanted to give her a little bracelet as a gift, a small gesture from my heart to hers. A little reminder of love, connection, and hope. I left feeling incredibly grateful, inspired, and touched by all the beautiful women I met today. Their stories reminded me that even in the hardest moments, there is still so much beauty, warmth, strength, and light. Because even in the darkest moments, hope shines through. 🩷🙏🏻

Dfund_rMU7c.caption:

Today, I wear pink with purpose. 🙏🏻💓

This is what missuniverse stands for, empowering women, amplifying voices, and creating a platform for meaningful change.

Today, through missuniverse missuniversenetherlands, I have the opportunity to turn that vision into action. To use my voice, my position, and this platform to advocate for change, bring important social issues to the forefront, and empower others to speak up.

Because to me, being missuniversenetherlands is about so much more than a title. It is about responsibility, representation, and using the platform you are given to create opportunities for others. And that is a purpose I am truly proud to stand for. ❤️✨

DfCDKZmDHXt.caption:
With only 11 days until my departure, I wanted to take a moment to reflect on this journey and express just how blessed and grateful I feel. Being missuniversenetherlands has given me the opportunity to do what matters most to me. Using my voice and platform to empower others. Through my campaign nowunmuted, I’ve been able to encourage women and children to speak up, share their stories, and find the courage to make their voices heard.

From serving as an ambassador for schoolenveiligheid during Anti-Bullying Week, visiting schools, and sharing my own experience with bullying on live television, to crossing borders and making an impact in Kenya. This journey has been so much more than I could have ever imagined.

Every single woman I’ve met in Kenya has left a lasting impact on me. Their strength, resilience, and determination have reminded me of the power of creating opportunities for women. Together with our partners and communities, we raised over €175,000. Funds that are helping women take on leadership roles, and create plans for the future of their own communities.

And of course, my team. The love and support you have given me mean so much to me, and I couldn’t have wished for a better team. To every person who has played a part in this journey, please know that I will be forever grateful. God bless you. 

And now, the Netherlands is ready! Ready to wear our national colour, orange, with pride. Bring the elegance and artistry of Vincent van Gogh, and embody the energy

De1JwTtsWZT.caption:
Impact goes beyond raising awareness. It is about creating opportunities, breaking barriers, and building a future where everyone has the chance to thrive. 

The Netherlands is home to one of the best water management systems in the world. Water is life, and the valuable lessons learned here are worth sharing beyond borders. From the Netherlands to Kenya, I hope to turn knowledge into meaningful action for a more sustainable future.

My time in Kenya reminded me how deeply something as fundamental as access to safe water can shape the lives of women and children. When accessing water takes hours every day, opportunities for education, independence and personal growth can become limited.

This is why SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, SDG 5: Gender Equality, and SDG 4: Quality Education are so deeply interconnected. Because access to safe water is not just about meeting a basic need. It is about protecting dignity, creating equal opportunities, and ensuring that women and children have the time and opportunity to pursue education and build their future. 

As Miss Universe Netherlands, I believe the responsibility of this platform goes far beyond the crown. Through our work with wateraidnl and my platform nowunmuted, I want to use my voice to amplify the voices of women and girls, raise awareness about the barriers they face, and help turn awareness into meaningful action.

Beyond the crown, there is a purpose. Beyond the title, there is a responsibility. And beyond the words,

DetNU4OsLpt.caption:
nowunmuted was born from my personal experience with bullying. I still remember being younger and wondering if it was normal for other children to call me weird or different. I was quiet, and I didn’t always have the confidence to stand up for myself. As I grew older, I realised that being bullied should never be considered normal, and that no one should ever feel less worthy for being who they are.

Today, I have made it my mission to use my voice to raise awareness about the lifelong impact of bullying and the importance of building confidence. Words matter. The things we say can leave lasting scars, but they can also inspire, empower, and change lives. I believe that speaking up is an act of courage and that, through education, we can empower the next generation to stand up against bullying, embrace their individuality, and believe that their dreams are valid, no matter how big they may be.

Through nowunmuted, I remind people that their voices matter, their differences are their strength, and their potential is limitless. You are worthy of taking up space, you are deserving of kindness, and you are capable of achieving anything you set your mind to. 🙏🏻✨

DeTsHALsYe8.caption:
Today is a reminder that it’s okay to talk about what’s going on inside, to ask for help, and to take care of your mental well-being. I chose this childhood photo of myself because it represents a part of my story that has had a lasting impact on my mental health. 

Growing up, I was bullied. At the time, I didn’t fully understand how deeply those experiences would affect me later in life. When I was 14, I started a psychological treatment journey and eventually also went through EMDR therapy to process some of the experiences I had been through. 

Looking back at this little girl, I wish I could tell her that none of it was her fault. That she was enough, that she was worthy, and that she will find the strength to heal.

Our mental health can be shaped by experiences that happened when we were young, sometimes in ways we only understand years later. So, on World Mental Health Day, I want to remind you: be kind to yourself, talk about what you’re going through, and don’t be afraid to ask for help. You never know the battles someone is quietly fighting. 🤎

#unmuted #nowunmuted #mentalhealthadvocate #mentalhealth #mentalhealthawareness

DdWtqGWDDUI.caption:
Today, I visited the Ntalala Women’s Group. For just a short moment, I carried a 20 kg jerry can on my back. Even for that brief moment, I could feel how heavy and difficult it is. But for these women, carrying water is part of their daily reality.

Thanks to wateraidnl the cause I have been proudly supporting, these women now only have to walk 10–45 minutes to access clean and safe drinking water. In the Netherlands, I walked 10 km across the Wadden Sea to raise awareness and funds for WaterAid. But being here today made me realise that those 10 kilometres were about so much more than the distance I walked. They were about helping create a future where women and children no longer have to spend hours every day walking for something as essential as clean water.

Meeting these strong and powerful women reminded me how fortunate we are and how easily we can take access to clean water for granted. Their strength and resilience are a powerful reminder that when we have a voice and an opportunity to make a difference, we should use them.

Because change starts with one step, one voice and one person choosing to make a difference. ❤️

DdWlsG6DEfT.caption: The innocence of a child is one of the purest things in this world, and it deserves to be cherished, protected, and loved. 🙏🏻

DdUX8LRDB90.caption:
Today, I had the privilege of visiting Enkaroni Primary School and speaking to these children about something that means so much to me. Being proud of who you are and never being afraid to embrace what makes you unique. I reminded them that kindness is a choice. Instead of bringing each other down, we should lift each other up, make one another feel seen, and create connections. 

After my speech, I challenged the children to choose someone they had barely, or maybe never, spoken to before and spend some time connecting through a fun activity. Watching them open up, laugh together, and step outside their comfort zones was truly beautiful. 

Their energy and enthusiasm touched my heart more than I can put into words. I came to share a message with them, but I left feeling like they had taught me something too. A moment I will cherish and carry with me for a lifetime. 🤎

Representing Falcón, 25-year-old medical student Sofía Pascuzzo (sofia_pascuzzo) was crowned Miss Venezuela World on Thursday, November 19, at Venevisión’s Studio 1 in Caracas. Ten contestants were eligible for the national title at the gala, which aired live on Venevisión and streamed on Venevisión Play and Miss Venezuela’s official YouTube channel. Sofía will represent Venezuela at Miss World 2027 in Tanzania. 

In a moving farewell filled with gratitude, Mística Núñez took her final walk before passing the crown to Sofía, marking a second consecutive win for Falcón. Mística was a Beauty With a Purpose finalist at Miss World in Vietnam with Semillas de Vida, her initiative to combat childhood malnutrition and support early childhood development in her home state. 

The new Miss World Venezuela brings a background in competitive sports and community volunteering to her new role. She recalls volunteering with a medical team in Caracas after the recent earthquake, where she helped support families affected by the crisis. She wants to use her platform to help children and teens in underserved communities access sports programs, nutrition education, and mental health support. 

Congratulations, Sofía! See you in Tanzania! 

#missworldvenezuela #missworld #beautywithapurpose #missworldintanzania #tanzaniaunforgettable

Zanzibar’s Minister of Tourism and Heritage, Dr. Nasra Nassor Omar, welcomed Julia Morley CBE, Miss World Joheirry Mola and the six Continental Winners to Park Hyatt Zanzibar in historic Stone Town for Press Conference. Julia spoke of her hope that the visit would lead to lasting work together for Zanzibar’s children. The seven titleholders each received a handcrafted replica of a traditional Zanzibari door, a welcome that celebrates Stone Town’s distinctive architecture and the artisans who keep its woodworking traditions alive.

Over the coming days, the titleholders will take turns reporting from across the island. Joheirry Mola will explore Stone Town’s heritage, Elisabeth Reynés will go diving, Georgia-Lee Gill will take us on a sunset cruise, and Tiarē Henry-Anguna will visit Zanzibar’s sandbanks. Romanda Hombir will meet the Mammas of Zanzibar, Gabriela Botelho will visit a spice farm, and Taanusiya Chetty will introduce us to a local seaweed farming community.

Follow along as they share Zanzibar through the stories of the people they meet.
