Df2wbHypREK.caption:
For the Miss Universe charity auction, I wanted to offer something that represents more than Latvia’s beauty. Something with history, identity and a story of its own.

The Crown of Kuldīga draws inspiration from the traditional bridal headdresses of Kuldīga and the Kurzeme region. Historically, these crowns were much more than ornaments. They were part of a woman’s identity, her traditions and important milestones in life.

Bringing this idea to life was the talented Latvian artisan Evita Vilde wildehandmade 💕.

I want to give special recognition to Evita, because it takes a truly special eye and skill to look at historical craftsmanship and transform it into something contemporary without losing its meaning. Every detail, from the golden band to the delicate blue embellishments, reflects her dedication, creativity and love for her craft.

I believe that artisans like Evita play an important role in keeping cultural heritage alive. They don’t simply recreate the past; they give it a future.

I am particularly proud that this gift will represent Latvia on an international stage, and that through this charity auction, a piece of our heritage can become part of something bigger.

Thank you, Evita, for your beautiful work and for putting so much of yourself into this creation.

A crown with a history. A craft with a future. A little piece of Latvia to share with the world. 🇱🇻

I want to encourage women to share their stories, speak openly, and never feel ashamed of being vulnerable. We don’t have to pretend that everything is perfect. Sometimes, simply knowing that someone understands can make all the difference.

We may all have different journeys, but we can give each other something incredibly valuable: understanding, kindness and support.

Ddld1zwodeG.caption:
I don’t think I ever realised how much food could affect your life until I was diagnosed with celiac disease.

For a long time, I simply thought I had a sensitive stomach. I was tired, uncomfortable, bloated, and often felt like my body was working against me. Food was something I had to think about all the time, but I didn’t understand why.

Then came the diagnosis.

And suddenly, something as simple as eating became a little more complicated.

Reading labels. Asking questions at restaurants. Learning that gluten can hide in places you would never expect. Being the person who brings her own food. Having to explain, again and again, that it isn’t a preference or a lifestyle choice.

But with time, I stopped seeing it as something that was taking things away from me.

I started learning my body instead.

I discovered new foods, new ways of cooking, fermentation, naturally gluten-free ingredients and little rituals around making food at home. I learned that nourishing yourself doesn’t have to feel restrictive.

And perhaps the biggest lesson has been this:

Your body is constantly speaking to you. Sometimes we just need to slow down enough to listen.

My celiac journey is still a journey. Some days are easy, some are not.

But I no longer see my body as something I need to fight.

I’m learning to take care of it — gently, patiently, and with much more love. 🤍

Are you celiac?

DdgCPx6oY8n.caption:
For a long time, I thought being a good mother meant giving everything of myself. Being there all the time. Putting my own dreams aside. Making sure my child had everything she needed — even if it meant forgetting what I needed.

But I don’t want my daughter to grow up believing that love means losing yourself.

I want her to see a mother who loves her deeply, but also loves her own life.

A mother who has dreams and is brave enough to follow them.
A mother who knows how to be happy.
A mother who takes care of herself without feeling guilty.
A mother who can start again when life doesn’t go as planned.

Because one day, she will create her own life.

And I hope when she looks back at her childhood, she doesn’t only remember what I did for her.

I hope she remembers the woman I was beside her.

And I hope she thinks:

My mother showed me that I don’t have to choose between being loved and being myself.

Maybe that is also part of raising a daughter — not only preparing her for the world, but showing her what kind of life she is allowed to create for herself. 🤍

DdRJ_ugoNfm.caption:
I was afraid to start over. I thought this was simply how life had to be. People around me would say how lucky I was, never really knowing the price I was paying every day.

I thought I was too weak, too dependent, too much in love to walk away. Until one day, I found the courage to stand up for myself.

And then everything crashed apart.

It felt like I was falling into pieces. People told me I was making a mistake. Some turned against me. There were moments when I questioned everything — but I didn’t allow myself to look back.

I chose to keep going.

And here I am today. Looking back, I know I would make the same choice all over again.

Because my biggest motivation was never to prove anything to anyone. It was knowing that I could never want that kind of life for my child.

Sometimes, starting over is not losing everything. Sometimes, it is finally choosing yourself — and showing your child what it means to choose a life that feels right. 🤍

DcwDwROI3Zp.caption:
Lately, I’ve been trying to create more moments where my child and I simply make things together. 🤍

I want her childhood to be filled with curiosity — not just with finished toys, but with materials, ideas and little possibilities.

I’ve started thinking about toys a little like I think about food: less processed, more ingredients. 🥰

Give a child some paper, fabric, clay, sticks, boxes, flowers, paint, a kitchen full of ingredients… and suddenly there are endless things to create.

I want her to grow up knowing that things don’t always have to be bought ready-made.
That a beautiful dress can be sewn.
That food can be made from simple ingredients.
That decorations can be created by hand.
That something broken can sometimes be repaired.
That imagination is a tool.

So I’m trying everything with her lately — cooking, crafting, decorating, baking, making little things from almost nothing.

Not because I want every day to be a Pinterest project. 😄
But because I want her to know the feeling of “I can make this.”

Maybe that’s one of the most beautiful things we can give our children. 🤍

The dalagang Filipina, reimagined. 🇵🇭

Growing up, we were taught to associate the Filipina with being mahinhin, graceful, modest, and soft-spoken. But our history tells a much bigger story. Filipino women have always been courageous, outspoken, and willing to stand up for what they believe in.

Wearing Rob Ortega, I wanted to celebrate both sides of that identity. The delicate lace, flowing chiffon, and playful feathers reflect the femininity we have long embraced, while the bold silhouette represents the freedom and confidence of the Filipina today.

To me, being a modern Filipina means honoring the women who came before us while having the courage to create our own path. We can be gentle without being passive, graceful without being silent, and feminine without ever compromising our principles.

Because there is strength in softness, and there is power in using our voice. 🤍

DduCBZxlFzR.caption:
🌎 GLOBAL GOALS DAY | SEPTEMBER 25

Behind every smile there is a person, a story, and a life worth caring for.

As a dentist and Miss International Chile, I have chosen to use my voice and my profession to create SMILES BEYOND BORDERS, a project rooted in something I deeply believe in: oral health is a right, and every person deserves the freedom to smile with dignity.

From teaching children how to prevent oral disease, to bringing care and education closer to older adults, and supporting people facing cancer through my work with Fundación Felipe Coloma, my purpose is to make oral health education, prevention and care reach those who need it most.

And this commitment goes beyond education.
I want to help provide free dental care and treatment to people who need it, because access to oral health should never be determined by someone’s circumstances. 

Because oral health is not only about teeth.
It is about being able to eat without pain.
To speak without shame.
To laugh freely.
To feel cared for.
And to never lose the power to smile. 

Today, on Global Goals Day, I reaffirm my commitment to SDG 3, Good Health and Well-Being, and to using my platform to turn awareness into action.

Because sometimes, creating change begins with something as simple as helping someone protect their smile.

Educate. Prevent. Treat. Empower.

And always remember:

When we open a smile, we open a future. 🌎✨

#SustainableDevelopmentGoals #BeautiesForSDGs #sdg

DgAcSUsGx7R.caption:
UGNAYAN. 🇵🇭

An archival piece by Rajo Laurel, rooted in the weaving traditions of the Cordillera.

UGNAYAN, meaning connection, draws from a braiding and weaving technique Rajo learned from renowned Cordillera weaver Narda Capuyan.

Individual strands of color and texture are intertwined, creating a dress that moves with every step. Beyond its craftsmanship, the piece speaks to something deeply Filipino: the ties that bind us through family, friendship, and community.

A beautiful reminder that even in the places life takes us, we remain connected to where we come from.

Tonight, I’m excited to share another expression of Filipino artistry on the Miss Universe stage. See you at the National Costume Show at 7 PM Puerto Rico time (7 AM Philippine time)! 🇵🇭💧

DgBgjQ8DFOa.caption:
DIWA NG KORDILYERA 🇵🇭

From the mountains of Northern Luzon, a celebration of the Cordillera’s rich and diverse Indigenous heritage.

A contemporary national costume inspired by the distinct cultural traditions of Kalinga and Mountain Province. The ensemble brings together Kalinga-inspired tattoo patterns, intricate beadwork, and the rich textile weaving traditions of Mountain Province, alongside a striking arrangement of earthen vessels inspired by the Banga Salidsid of Kalinga.

The Banga Salidsid pays tribute to the stamina, strength, and grace of Kalinga women who traditionally navigated steep mountain paths and rice terraces to fetch water for their communities. The balancing of earthen vessels becomes a powerful expression of resilience and the important role of women in sustaining everyday life.

Beyond its cultural inspiration, the costume also carries a message of environmental responsibility. As changing climate conditions continue to threaten water security, we hope to raise awareness of the importance of clean and reliable water access, particularly for remote communities across the Philippine archipelago.

A contemporary interpretation honoring the artistry, craftsmanship, and living traditions of the Cordilleran peoples.

A heritage worth carrying, a story worth sharing with the world. 🇵🇭

DgCIKUKNPx2.caption:
It had been a while since Joheirry Mola last picked up a microphone to report a story. For the former Univision 41 New York reporter, taking viewers through the streets of Stone Town was a chance to relive something she loved doing. A little nostalgic and a lot of fun, this time the story took her to the historic heart of Zanzibar.

A UNESCO World Heritage Site, Stone Town grew as a Swahili trading port on the Indian Ocean. Centuries of exchange with the Arab world, India, and Europe helped shape its architecture, and some of the finest details are right at street level. Look closely at the famous Zanzibar doors and you’ll see how much care went into carving their wooden panels and frames. 

That attention to detail carries through to the work of Zanzibar’s artisans today. In the shops tucked into Stone Town’s narrow lanes, you’ll find handmade jewelry by local makers, another way to get to know the island through the things people create here. 

Come along with Joheirry as she takes us through Stone Town, from its winding streets and carved doors to the tanzanite jewelry she discovers along the way.

And of course, no visit to Stone Town would be complete without mentioning Freddie Mercury. The legendary Queen frontman was born right here in Zanzibar, and you can still visit his childhood home.

DgENzI1DKX2.caption:
THE GOLDEN SEAS OF SULU 🇵🇭

For my preliminary evening gown, I wanted to celebrate a different side of the Philippines, one that honors the rich cultural heritage and extraordinary marine biodiversity of Mindanao.

Inspired by the historic waters of the Sulu Sea, where centuries of maritime trade and cultural exchange have shaped the communities of our southern islands, the gown brings together intricate gold and deep blue beadwork. The radiating gold embellishments pay homage to Mindanao’s ancient traditions of gold craftsmanship, while the shimmering blues reflect the waters that are home to some of the Philippines’ richest marine ecosystems.

Every detail is an interpretation of the sea, from the way the beadwork catches the light to the fluid movement of the silhouette, reminiscent of the currents beneath the surface.

More than its beauty, I wanted this gown to honor the generations of artistry, the communities whose lives are connected to these waters, and the marine life we have a responsibility to protect.

A tribute to the cultural and natural treasures of the southern Philippines.

DgE0qQ0hFcw.caption:
Today at rehearsals I cried because I had a moment of frustration. 🥹

I received my dress after my coach bobbykaanjosa had left so we didn’t get a chance to physically create a routine in it so we decided that I would do a reveal with my over skirt and then drop it.

3 hours to the show, we were told that we were not allowed to drop any garment as it would interfere with the flow of the production.

In that moment I had to choose between keeping it on me the whole time or not wearing it at all. We had worked too hard on it for me not to showcase it.

I had never practiced walking with the over skirt and I did not want to just do a normal walk down so our choreographer here calmed me down and asked me to try and do the twirl while switching my hands for the cape. I only got once chance to try it before show time.

When I got off stage I was so eager to see a video and was almost in tears yet again because I was so proud of the execution. 🥹😭

Thank you so much gabrielapellot for capturing this moment.

Miss World Africa Romanda Hombir takes you along for a morning with the Mamas of Zanzibar! 

The Mamas welcomed Miss World Joheirry Mola and the continental winners into their home, helped them wrap themselves in colorful khangas, and walked with them to Chuini Market to pick out ingredients for lunch. DgFhNIxqwsZ.caption:
THE ART OF THE RICE TERRACES. 🇵🇭

A striking interpretation of the Philippine Cordilleras by Filipino designer Mark Bumgarner.

Drawing inspiration from the iconic rice terraces, Mark translates the landscape’s cascading formations into architectural pleats and fluid draping. Rendered in a vibrant shade of chartreuse, the gown captures the lush greenery and layered contours of our highlands, bringing a distinctly contemporary perspective to one of the Philippines’ most remarkable cultural landscapes.

Beyond the silhouette is a story that resonates with my advocacy for environmental conservation and the preservation of our natural and cultural heritage. The rice terraces are a testament to generations of Filipino ingenuity, craftsmanship, and the communities that continue to sustain them.

A celebration of our landscape, our heritage, and our shared responsibility to protect our Motherland. To preserve not only its natural beauty, but also the history, traditions, and communities that make it our home.

One day before the finals. Para sa Pilipinas. 🇵🇭

DgG9RJxjBOL.caption:
THE ART OF THE RICE TERRACES. 🇵🇭

The rice terraces represent more than the beauty of our landscapes. They are living expressions of our heritage, shaped by generations of Indigenous communities whose knowledge, traditions, and relationship with the land continue to sustain them.

Wearing this creation by Mark Bumgarner reminds me that protecting our environment also means respecting the people who have cared for it long before us. Our ancestral lands are not simply places to be admired; they are homes, histories, and identities that deserve recognition and protection.

As someone who believes in environmental conservation, I hope we continue to listen to Indigenous communities, respect their rights over their ancestral lands, and protect the natural and cultural heritage they have preserved for generations.

Proud to carry this story with me. One day before the finals, and every step is for the Philippines. 🇵🇭

A moment of repose and reflection with my eyes fixed squarely on the horizon 🌊

As I prepare to carry my beloved Philippines across my heart in the international arena, I want to take a moment to contemplate legacy. The 75th edition of Miss Universe is an opportunity to pay tribute to the women who have paved the way before me. To recognize that I am standing on the shoulders of giants who have used the crown to change the world for good; Gloria Diaz, Margie Moran, Pia Wurtzbach, Catriona Gray. 

It is also an opportunity to forge a new path forward. Growing up deeply connected to our oceans, and now representing one of the most climate vulnerable countries in the world, I not only carry the voices of 118 million Filipinos to the international stage, I also urge the international community to reflect on the kind of world we will leave behind. To care for our oceans, our environment, and our planet is an act of love and compassion for our children and our children’s children. 

The 75th Miss Universe is a celebration of past, present, and future. Using the lessons of the women who led before us to guide our present course towards a brighter and kinder future.

DgIKUM4plX_.caption:
Three looks. Three stories. One journey to the Miss Universe stage. 🇱🇻

Behind every look, there is a little piece of me.

The swimsuit represents my relationship with my body. For years, I have been training and trying to maintain a healthy weight, which has been a challenge as my weight tends to drop and I struggle to gain it back. Motherhood brought many physical changes, and just before flying to this competition, I found out I needed an operation. So, stepping onto that stage is also about appreciating my body for everything it has carried me through — not striving for perfection.

The evening gown is my way of bringing Latvia onto the international stage. Inspired by our national flag, its burgundy red and white represent my roots and identity. Created through a beautiful collaboration between Louis Tran from Vietnam and Evita Vilde from Latvia, it brings together cultures, craftsmanship and creativity. The cape, adorned with more than 5,000 feathers, adds a little magic to every step.

And finally, LAIMA — Where Fate Meets Freedom, my national costume. Inspired by Latvian mythology and traditions, every detail tells a story of our heritage. The three stars represent Latvia’s historical regions, the golden rays the sun, and the ears of rye our land. At its heart are Laima, representing fate, and Milda, representing freedom.

DgIAuy1t_fe.caption:
Miss World Americas Gabriela Botelho takes us inside a spice farm in Zanzibar, where Miss World Joheirry Mola and the six Continental Winners followed local guides to discover how spices grow, what they smell like fresh and how they helped shape the islands’ history.

Imagine sailing across the Indian Ocean to buy a spice no bigger than your fingernail! In the 1800s, traders came to Zanzibar for cloves, and those tiny buds helped turn the islands into a busy trading hub.

For Gabriela, the cloves brought to mind a Brazilian birthday favorite, the beijinho. If you’ve ever wondered what that little thing on top of the coconut sweet is, that’s a whole clove! The seven titleholders also got to choose spice-infused beauty products to take home as gifts.

Coming to Tanzania for Miss World 2027? Take a spice tour in Zanzibar and see which scent brings back a memory of your own.

Born in the United States to a Haitian mother and a Jamaican father, and shaped by my experiences living in the United States, France and Ghana, I am a third-culture kid who has learned to see the beauty in our differences and the humanity in our shared experiences.

Tonight, I proudly represent Haiti with a narrative that extends beyond resilience. We are a nation not only defined by what we have overcome, but by our brilliance, creativity, intellect, talent and extraordinary potential.

Haiti deserves to be celebrated not only for its strength in adversity, but for its excellence and its contributions to the world.

As a storyteller and multicultural advocate, I am ready to use my voice, my education and my global experiences to tell the untold stories, amplify the unheard voices and build bridges across cultures.

To me, Miss Universe is more than a crown. It is a responsibility to listen, to lead, to inspire and to ensure that every story, regardless of where it begins, has a place on the world stage.

I am rooted in my heritage, shaped by the world, and ready to serve the universe.

Tonight, I stand with faith in God, confidence in my preparation, and conviction in my purpose.

Haiti let us show the world not only how beautifully we rise, but how brilliantly we shine.🇭🇹👑

Anything can happen when preparation meets purpose and faith meets opportunity.

DgIaNgxJz5W.caption:
A month I will remember for a lifetime. 🤍

As my Miss Universe journey comes to an end, I find myself reflecting on everything this experience has taught me.

What I value most is the challenge itself. The preparation pushed me to change, adapt and grow in areas I had never even considered before. And I love that — experiences that take you beyond your comfort zone and help you discover new sides of yourself.

One of the most precious parts has been the people. Meeting women who share my values and building genuine friendships. I am especially grateful for Estonia, Moldova and my lovely roommate Kenya. I love you girls! 🤍

It has also been an incredibly demanding month. Endless waiting hours, sleepless nights, rehearsals, stage experiences, a whole new level of online presence and the responsibility of representing not only myself but my country.

I got sick and missed part of the experience, but perhaps it was also the rest my body desperately needed. Between irregular meals, little sleep and almost no personal time, the physical demands were real. I lost weight, muscle strength and quite a bit of energy along the way.

Behind all the beautiful gowns and glamorous moments, there is another side of this experience that few get to see.

I wish I had discovered more of Puerto Rico. This beautiful country has truly inspired me, and I know I will return to explore it properly. 💕

To everyone who supported me with kind words, messages, encouragement and helping hands — thank you.

DgJhSiMDOFW.caption:
PEARL OF THE ORIENT 🇵🇭

A tribute to Inang Bayan.

For my finale gown, I wanted to honor the Philippines, the Pearl of the Orient Seas.

Designed by Anthony Ramirez, the gown takes inspiration from the pristine white shores of the Visayas, particularly the island of Cebu.

Rendered in luminous ivory, the gown reflects the beauty of Cebu’s white sand beaches, intricately adorned with mother of pearl handpicked from its shores. Each piece was individually crafted into delicate seashells, corals, and pawikan motifs, the latter holding a special place in my heart as a reflection of my advocacy for marine conservation.

Thousands of iridescent embellishments capture the shimmer of sunlight across our seas, while sweeping chiffon panels bring a sense of movement and fluidity to the silhouette.

At the back, a sun motif inspired by the Philippine flag symbolizes our independence, resilience, and the enduring spirit of the Filipino people.

From the white shores of the Visayas to the sun that unites our nation, every detail is a tribute to Inang Bayan.

To Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. To the seas that connect our islands, and the beauty, heritage, and people that make us Filipino.

One nation. Thousands of islands. A beauty that is distinctly Filipino. 🇵🇭

DgOsKkNNoPD.caption:
“It feels like being in a movie!” 🦒🇹🇿

That’s how Tiarē Henry-Anguna of the Cook Islands, Miss World Oceania, described her day in Arusha National Park. And when a group of giraffes came within a few steps of the group, it was easy to see what she meant.

Miss World 2026 Joheirry Mola, the six Continental Winners and Miss World Tanzania spotted buffalo, monkeys, including what looked like a blue monkey, and a warthog with its little ones. Yes, a real-life Pumbaa! We also took in a waterfall tumbling between rock formations, but for Georgia-Lee Gill of Trinidad and Tobago, Miss World Caribbean, it was seeing a giraffe so close that brought tears to her eyes.

They stopped for lunch at Hatari Lodge (hatari.travel), where the team welcomed them with a delicious meal featuring local flavors, all gluten-free. Between the beautiful setting and the warm hospitality, it was a lovely place to sit down together and trade stories from the morning.

It was also Miss World Tanzania’s first day with the group. She and the other titleholders hit it off right away as they reunited, and she took pride in sharing more about her country as they explored Arusha together.

The day in Arusha National Park ended in the late afternoon on the shores of Lake Momella.

The team at Gosheni Safaris drove the titleholders through Arusha National Park and expertly guided them throughout the day.

DgQ4cwrDa9z.caption:
Merci pour tout. 🤍

Représenter la France à Miss Universe était un rêve immense. Cette aventure ne s’est pas déroulée exactement comme je l’avais imaginée : ma blessure au genou a tout bouleversé et il y a eu des moments de doute et de frustration. Mais j’ai continué avec détermination jusqu’au bout, entourée par mon équipe, mes proches et tous vos messages, dont le soutien m’a énormément touchée.

Durant cette aventure, j’ai essayé de me dévoiler sincèrement et de vous montrer différentes facettes de qui je suis. J’espère avoir inspiré certaines jeunes filles qui, comme moi autrefois, peuvent être timides, douter d’elles-mêmes ou ne pas oser se lancer.

Ne laissez personne étouffer votre voix ni vous dicter qui vous devriez être. Croyez en vous et osez, toujours avec bienveillance et gentillesse, car notre monde en a profondément besoin.

Je repars avec des souvenirs inoubliables, une force nouvelle et une immense fierté d’avoir représenté mon pays. Merci pour tout l’amour que vous m’avez donné. 🤍

—

DgRPbMalDSz.caption:
Creativity and Sustainability

For this activity, my mom and I created a dress using recycled materials.

We visited a bookstore and asked if they had any old books that were going to be recycled. We collected those books and started bringing our idea to life, creating the base of the dress and turning recycled paper into something beautiful.

Then, I had a photoshoot wearing our creation to raise awareness about sustainability and show that we don't always need to buy an expensive, elegant dress to create something special.

Sometimes, all we need is imagination, creativity, and the willingness to give materials a second life.

Because fashion can also be sustainable, and small creative actions can inspire big changes. 🌎♻️

Isabella Bermúdez Nieto | Miss Earth Colombia 2026

Miss World Joheirry Mola, Julia Morley CBE, the six Continental Winners and Miss World Tanzania set out from Arusha for a day on safari. DgSyfcnmrl-.caption:
There are experiences in life that change you in ways words could never fully capture. Representing Canada on the Miss Universe stage was one of them. 🤍

There is so much to a journey like this that goes unseen. This experience challenged me in ways I hadn’t anticipated, but through the moments of doubt, growth and self-discovery, I learned that there is so much more to be gained from an experience than its outcome.

I hope that in sharing my journey, I have inspired others to dream a little bigger, believe in themselves a little more and never compromise who they are in pursuit of their dreams.
There is still so much to reflect on and share, but I leave this experience with beautiful friendships, invaluable lessons and immense pride in having represented my country.

For now, I’ll simply say thank you, Canada, for the honour of a lifetime. 🤍
